findings.reason: naming those owners up front would replace the new class with an extension of the owner rather than a parallel one.
findings.text: the section adds a service subsystem with no reuse map, though `reckon/service.py` already renders, installs and controls user units and `paid_lanes.systemd_user_dir()` already owns where a unit lives

findings.reason: two unit managers drift; the plan should extend `reckon/service.py` with a per-project unit name and render instead of forking a second manager.
findings.text: `SystemdUserWatchService` reimplements `reckon/service.py`'s `unit_path` (service.py:89), `installed` (service.py:217), `write_unit` (service.py:230), `systemctl` (service.py:180) and `linger_enabled`/`enable_linger` (service.py:201,207), and its `write_unit` line 3461 copies the unchanged-content write logic of `service.write_unit` verbatim, including the "systemd opens the log file but will not create its parent" step

findings.reason: path resolution is the recurring duplicate this item names; with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` set the watcher writes to one directory while the manager reads another, so the unit never starts.
findings.text: `SystemdUserWatchService.unit_path` hardcodes `Path.home() / ".config" / "systemd" / "user"`, bypassing `paid_lanes.systemd_user_dir()` (paid_lanes.py:750) which resolves `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` the way systemd itself does

findings.reason: it would add a fourth resolution site; the plan should name one owner that both `store_review` and `check-manifest` (whose `audit_manifest`, reports.py:1858, already sits beside a resolver) call, folding the existing pair in.
findings.text: §60 has `store_review` resolve `reviewed_base_sha`/`reviewed_head_sha`, where commit resolution is already owned by `promotion._commit_resolves_in` (promotion.py:477) and `reports._commit_resolves_in` (reports.py:1494) — two copies already — and `recovery._resolve_commit` (recovery.py:378)

findings.reason: the honest change is to parameterise the existing renderer and installer for a named unit rather than add a parallel class.
findings.text: the new `SystemdUserWatchService` wraps `reckon/service.py`'s machinery without saying why `reckon/service.py` cannot be extended to render and install a second unit

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no module that hides substantial behaviour behind a smaller interface; the §3 facade is over-wrapping, reported under thin_wrapper and duplicate_owner.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 forks `reckon/service.py`'s unit manager and bypasses `paid_lanes.systemd_user_dir()`; §60 adds a further commit resolver beside three existing ones.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §3 introduces `SystemdUserWatchService` without citing `reckon/service.py`, which already renders, installs and controls user units.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3's `SystemdUserWatchService` is a thin layer over `reckon/service.py` and `paid_lanes`, with no statement of why those owners cannot be extended.
